10133-the-vigil-of-venus-and-other-poems:
Q, the pen name of Arthur Quiller-Couch, published this 1912 volume, dedicating it to Maurice Hewlett with a sailor's salute, ship to ship. The title poem, The Vigil of Venus, renders the ancient Pervigilium Veneris, a spring night-song to the goddess of love.

Other poems include a one-act drama, The Regent, Exmoor verses, Vashti's song, two folk songs, The Soldier, The Marine, Mary Leslie, Jenifer's love, two duets, and a chant royal of high virtue. Q writes with learning and music. Readers get a varied, craftsmanlike book of verse from a master anthologist.
39592-princess-mary-s-gift-book-all-prof:
Princess Mary's Gift Book sold its pages for a wartime relief fund. All gains from sale went to the Queen's Work for Women Fund. That fund worked hand in hand with the National Relief Fund. Hodder and Stoughton put the book out in London and New York. Princess Mary thanks the writers and artists in her own signed note.

Names of the first rank gave tales and art to the gift book. Barrie opens it with A Holiday in Bed and Brock's drawings. Hall Caine, Ralph Connor, and Conan Doyle all gave short pieces. Fabre writes on the ant-lion with Detmold art at its side. Rackham art lights a tale of a land of make-believe. Paintings and drawings crowd the book from page to page.
47577-the-jesuit-relations-and-allied-do:
Volume four of The Jesuit Relations and Allied Documents, printed at Cleveland in 1897, covers Acadia and Quebec from 1616 to 1629. Reuben Gold Thwaites edited the great series for the Burrows Brothers. The volumes print the French, Latin and Italian texts beside English translations. A portrait of Jean de Brébeuf fronts this one.

The chief document is the end of Pierre Biard's Relation of New France, printed at Lyons in 1616. Its last chapters tell of the English pillage of the mission's ship and goods. Letters by Charles Lalemant follow, written from Kebec in 1625 and 1626. One letter, sent from Bordeaux in 1629, closes the set. Notes and bibliographical data fill the back.
61105-begin-to-knit-all-the-basic-stitch:
Begin to Knit is Star Book number 201 of the American Thread Company, priced at twenty-nine cents. Its cover promises all the basic stitches, easy novelty stitches, and quick things to make, worked in Dawn yarns. An alphabetical contents runs from abbreviations, an afghan, and a baby set through casting on, gauge, left-hand knitting, and the garter stitch, to socks, slipovers, a poncho, and a raglan sweater.

The fundamentals page warns beginners to buy all yarn at once, since dye lots differ in shade, and explains ply as the strands twisted together. There are only three basic stitches, the book insists: knit, purl, and slip; all others come from variations and yarn overs. Tips cover winding wool, needle types, markers, and holders. The book is a newsstand teacher for the postwar knitting boom, brisk and encouraging.
74098-war-no-81-q:
War Number 81-Q is a science fiction story by Cordwainer Smith, the pen name of Paul Linebarger. The story first appeared in The Adjutant, volume nine, number one, of June 1928. It was Linebarger first published story, printed in a high school publication of his youth. A note says the tale was later rewritten, and this is the original version.

The plot opens with a war made by permit between Tibet and America in the year 2127. Each side claims the Radiant Heat Monopoly, and the Universal War Board grants the war permit with conditions. Five aero ships of twenty two thousand tons, part plane and part dirigible, are to be the only combatants. The schoolboy author, son of a diplomat, already shows the odd, rule bound future wars that the mature Cordwainer Smith would make famous in his stories.
doe-osti-2574068-next-generation-paramet:
Final technical report DE-SC0019461, led by Archana Kamal at the University of Massachusetts Lowell and covering September 2021 to March 2025, reports the PIQUE 2.0 program. PIQUE uses parametric interactions, drives that couple qubits through a modulated link, to create and control quantum states in Josephson junction circuits. Partners Raytheon-BBN, NIST Boulder, and the Air Force Research Laboratory in Rome, New York, ran the experimental side.

Three objectives organized the work: co-designing multi-qubit entanglement, time-dependent control of dissipation, and entanglement of qudits, units holding more than two levels. Results include a first-principles theory of parametric circuit quantum electrodynamics. The team also built reservoir engineering schemes that use bath correlations, and protocols that stabilize W-type entanglement across many qubits with only polynomial growth in settling time. The theory was extended to high-dimensional entangled states of qudits as well.
doe-osti-2999892-maturing-ceramic-am-and:
Kwan-Soo Lee, Ryan Wilkerson, Kim Trinh and Jihyeon Kim report in LA-UR-25-30484, issued 22 October 2025, on maturing ceramic 3D printing at Los Alamos National Laboratory. Printed ceramics could replace syntactic foams, hollow-bead plastics used as light structural fillers, if the printed parts can be made strong and predictable. The project also builds the qualification framework, the test ladder a printed part must climb before real use.

Trials used a porcelain resin sold by Tethon3D. Bars printed in three build directions survived firing without cracks, and the 4-millimetre build direction bent strongest in four-point tests. Lattices in four patterns, simple cubic, body-centred cubic, gyroid and fluorine, were tuned for exposure and heat. A simple cubic lattice with 6-millimetre cells reached compressive strengths of 5.63 to 6.94 megapascals at low density. Firing shrinkage ran about 4 percent across and 5 to 6 percent upward, numbers designers must build into their models.
doe-osti-3000318-preparation-for-dm-sear:
Fabio Castaneda, a University of Padua student working with Fermilab's SQMS centre, reports in FERMILAB-TM-2866-STUDENT, dated 14 October 2024, on groundwork for two dark matter hunts. Both use haloscopes: ultra-quiet resonant cavities, cooled near absolute zero, where dark matter particles might convert into a faint power excess. Their superconducting cavities boast quality factors near a hundred million, so a whisper of signal can build up.

For the SERAPH experiment, Castaneda helped characterise the cavity at millikelvin temperatures and then analysed the data collected. SERAPH targets candidates such as dark photons with an open-ended cylindrical cavity and a sliding plunger for tuning. For the SHADE experiment, still in preparation, he built a flexible analysis framework starting from simulated data. Supervisor Bianca Giaccone oversaw the work. The report captures the unglamorous calibration stage on which any discovery claim will rest.
doe-osti-3018055-compositing-and-charact:
Richard C Daniel, Carolyn A Burns, and Amy M Westesen of Pacific Northwest National Laboratory led this December 2025 report on compositing and characterizing waste exemplars from Hanford's Southeast Quadrant. Six authors are named in all. Tank waste varies enormously from tank to tank, so experiments need blended samples, called exemplars, that stand in for a whole region's waste.

The report covers waste selection and compositing strategy, then receipt and compositing of the samples themselves. Characterization followed, measuring how the blended material behaves. One thread tracked settling: rates were computed by regressing settled volumes against time, and settling ran largely linear until volumes neared their final state. Knowing the starting concentration of solids in suspension was essential to that math. Process designers get blended waste whose pedigree is documented, so test results can be traced back to the tanks they represent.
doe-osti-3024758-new-approaches-to-bayes:
Chun Shen reports project DE-SC0024232 on new Bayesian methods for uncertainty quantification in nuclear science. Inverse problems sit everywhere in the field: experimenters measure effects and must infer the causes, with honest error bars. Bayesian inference gives a clean way to do that, but nuclear problems carry many parameters and heavy computing costs, so faster tools are needed.

The proposal behind the report joins nuclear scientists on flagship efforts, neutrino mass measurement, quark-gluon plasma studies, and radiation environment mapping. Data scientists build the methods alongside. Activity lists show the machinery in use: talks on Gaussian process emulators for nuclear physics and equation-of-state generation. A three-dimensional-plus-time Bayesian analysis of RHIC beam energy scan data, presented at Argonne in October 2024.
nasa-tm-19680009561-initial-results-of-s:
Thomas C. O'Bryan, at the Langley Research Center in Virginia, reported early handling studies for the Moon landing in January 1966. Apollo's landing maneuver had no earthly parallel, he notes. Pilots would fly a rocket vehicle in weak gravity with no air at all.

The final descent is often compared with a helicopter landing approach. O'Bryan stresses how different the lunar case really is. The Moon's low gravity and missing atmosphere change the feel completely. His paper gives first results from a simulator facility built for lunar landing control. It also describes that facility, which let pilots practice the strange task safely.
podcast-dannyjones-T501LHx0R_Q:
Two researchers, Len Ber and Robert Duncan, join Danny Jones to argue that CIA mind control weapons are not history but current practice. Duncan has written on directed energy and neurotechnology for years, and together they present cases of people who report electronic harassment and voice-to-skull effects they attribute to secret programs.

Jones asks for the technical basis and the documents, and the guests supply what they have: patents, program fragments, and testimony. The claims are not established, and the symptoms described have other explanations that medicine offers and the guests reject. The episode preserves the targeted-individual literature in its most credentialed presentation. Listeners meet a belief community's best case, stated by its own researchers, and can judge how it handles the demand for proof.
podcast-dannyjones-_cq6GkM99_Q:
Author Tom O'Neill joins Danny Jones to argue that the CIA ran secret mind control tests on Charles Manson. O'Neill spent years on a book about the Manson case and the files around it. His claim ties the cult leader to agency programs.

O'Neill walks through the files, the doctors, and the odd links he found between Manson and state programs. He argues the known story of the cult hides a darker one. Jones asks how much rests on paper and how much on guess. Listeners get a deep, strange retelling of a famous crime. The library holds the talk as an archive record.
the-vigil-of-venus-and-other-poems-by-q: Q published The Vigil of Venus and Other Poems in 1912, dedicating the volume to Maurice Hewlett in a verse letter. The two poets are compared there to ships dipping ensigns, carrying ballads and woven tales as freight. Only the dedication poem and contents are present in this record, so the title poem itself does not appear. Contents entries name the Vigil of Venus with its Latin title Pervigilium Veneris, and a one-act drama called The Regent. A poems section includes Exmoor verses, Vashti's Song, Saturn, and a coronation hymn.
